column1: # Standalone-inference rows that do NOT work on the pinned toolchain, and why.
# Read by the "Assert standalone inference results" step. Any row not listed here must pass, with
# the backend it resolved and a real execution_path both asserted. A row listed here must FAIL, and
# fail with the named cause — if it starts passing, or fails for a different reason, the job goes
# red and says so. These are recorded limitations, not silenced ones.
# Toolchain: TornadoVM v6.0.0, which pom.xml declares (tornadovm.base.version), built from its tag
# by .github/actions/setup-tornadovm.
# Columns, tab-separated:
#   backend  model  quantization  configuration  cause-substring
# Every row this table used to carry was a symptom of the TornadoVM release pin, not of this
# project. Moving the pin from v5.2.0-jdk21 to v6.0.0 removed both causes at once.
# Cause A — batch-prefill-decode died in TornadoVM's interpreter with
#   NullPointerException: XPUDeviceBufferState.getXPUBuffer() is null
#   at TornadoVMInterpreter.executeAlloc
# In 5.2.0, consumeFromDevice(producerName, ...) ignored the name and resolved against whichever
# graph ran *previously*, then imported that graph's device buffer unconditionally. The batched
# plan revisits graphs (prefill layers -> decodeActivation -> decode layers -> logits ->
# decodeActivation -> ...), so from the SECOND decode pass on, decode layer 0 imported
# decodeActivation's null buffer for wrapKeyCache/wrapValueCache/wrapBlockTable and the next ALLOC
# dereferenced it. The first decode token always succeeded, which is why this looked like a
# mid-generation crash rather than a wiring fault. Fixed upstream in 8603a9fa2d ("Fix
# consumeFromDevice silently reading a stale buffer when the named producer is not the previously
# executed graph", PR #996): producers now resolve by name, and both the import and the
# pre-allocated-size lookup are guarded against a producer that has not run.
# It was never Metal-specific — the code path is backend-independent, and this table's own previous
# revision recorded it on cuda and opencl too. The earlier "works on CUDA, fails on Metal" reading
# came from comparing a locally installed SDK that already carried the fix against a tag-source
# build that did not. That also settles the discrepancy the previous revision flagged as unresolved.
# Cause B — the FP16 sketch-phase failure:
#   TornadoBailoutRuntimeException: Unable to build sketch for method: <kernel>
#   ([ERROR] Class reader could not be instantiated for class file: java/lang/invoke/LambdaForm$MH...)
# TornadoVM's ASM visitor failing to read a JVM-synthesized hidden class. Recorded by task 6 as
# fixed on TornadoVM's development line but not in 5.2.0; 6.0.0 is the release that carries it.
# Measured on an Apple M4 Pro against a v6.0.0 tag build, all 14 locally reproducible metal rows —
# Llama-3.2-1B F16 and Q8_0, Qwen3-0.6B F16 and Q8_0 across standard / prefill-decode /
# batch-prefill-decode, plus Mistral-7B Q8_0 and a Qwen2.5 F16 — pass, including every metal row
# this table used to list.
# The cuda and opencl legs run on Linux and could NOT be verified locally (a Mac's OpenCL is
# Apple's own implementation, not the one CI uses), and neither could the metal rows for models
# not held locally (Phi-3-mini, Granite, Qwen2.5-1.5B). Those rows are cleared on the strength of
# both causes being backend-independent runtime/compiler-frontend fixes, which is a prediction
# rather than a measurement. This job is the check: any row that still fails will go red and name
# its own cause, which is exactly what the table is for. Re-record a row here only with its
# observed cause substring, never pre-emptively.
# Running --opencl on macOS fails for Qwen3 (both F16 and Q8_0, every configuration) with
#   clCreateKernel(processHeadsFlashAttentionSplitKVPaged) failed: CL error -48 (CL_INVALID_KERNEL)
#   UNSUPPORTED (log once): createKernel: newComputePipelineState failed
# That is Apple's OpenCL-over-Metal shim refusing the paged flash-attention kernel; the same model
# and kernel run correctly on metal. It does not affect CI, whose opencl leg is Linux, so it has no
# row here — but it will bite anyone benchmarking --opencl on a Mac.
# Phi-3-mini does not complete on Metal in CI. Both rows are host memory, not a kernel defect,
# and the earlier note here ("a real hang with no diagnostic") was wrong about the cause:
#   * The Mac runner is an Apple M4 reporting 11.8 GB of Metal memory, so a 16 GB machine.
#     Apple Silicon is unified: a device buffer is host RAM.
#   * Measured on an M4 Pro at the CI row's own -n 160, Phi-3-mini-Q8_0 peaks at 9.5 GiB RSS,
#     and F16 carries roughly 3.7 GiB more of weights on top of that. The heap size does not
#     move either number (8g and 20g both measure 9.5 GiB), so this is off-heap unified memory
#     and not a JVM heap that could be tuned down.
#   * Genuine over-capacity is NOT what this looks like. A model that truly does not fit fails
#     in ~30 s with [GPUL-MEM-001] DeviceMemoryExhaustedException, verified on Qwen3-8B-F16.
#     These rows instead swap: correct tokens arrive, then progress stops. That is the
#     signature of thrashing, which is why no exception is ever raised.
# Until run 33996905843 a timed-out row also leaked its JVM -- the runner killed the
# llama-tornado wrapper and not its java grandchild, leaving a process measured at 16.1 GiB RSS
# alive for the rest of the job on a 16 GB machine. That is fixed in .github/actions/
# run-inference (the kill goes to the process group), so the Q8_0 row now gets an unstarved
# machine and may well pass. If it does, this job fails with "NEW PASS" and its line below is
# to be deleted -- that is the table working, not a regression.
# The F16 row is expected to stay blocked on a 16 GB runner. It is a machine-size limit,
# recorded so the other Metal rows stay enforceable; it is not an accepted defect.
